── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: 6.8, 7.3 km
This week: 2.8 km over 1 run. Missed 2 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "Came down with a cold on Tuesday that turned into a fever, 38.4 on Wednesday night. No fever since Friday but still coughing and blocked up."
Feeling: "Wiped out."
Asks: "Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: You were right to skip Wednesday and Saturday with the fever. …
Answers: (1) No. Stick to your usual three days and don't add the two you missed. (2) Squeezing five sessions into one week would pile on work just when you can handle it least. Missed runs don't need to be paid back. (3) Next week is a walk on Monday, then two walk-runs. Wednesday's is shorter than usual.
Safety flag: Stop and get checked if warning signs appear
Safety flag: See a doctor if the cough hangs on
Next week:
Mon: other, 20 min walk at an easy pace on a flat route, no running. Tests your chest…
Tue: rest. Keep the dog walk short and gentle. Getting over the cold comes first.
Wed: easy, 18 min walk-run: 6 rounds of 2 min running and 1 min walking, flat route, run…
Thu: rest. A full day to see how your body handles the first run back.
Fri: rest. Your usual second rest day before the weekend run.
Sat: easy, 24 min walk-run: 8 rounds of 2 min running and 1 min walking, flat route…
Sun: rest. Finishes the week rested so the build can start again the week after.
